name: ShieldXen – Malware Scanner & Site Security Audit
author: InfinityTechCare

sections.description:
ShieldXen checks your site from the inside and tells you, in plain words, what to fix first.

What it checks

  • Files. Compares WordPress, your plugins and your themes with the official copies, looks for malware signatures, PHP hidden in images or where it doesn’t belong, backups and logs anyone could download, and old copies of WordPress left in the site. For your own code, which has no official copy, it reports changes nobody declared.
  • The database. Scripts and spam hidden in posts, widgets and settings, administrators and plugins hidden from their screens, accounts and application passwords added behind your back, code stored in options, snippets and scheduled tasks, and triggers that recreate an attacker’s account.
  • Your own code. Plugins and themes that aren’t on wordpress.org or from a known vendor get quick checks for the mistakes attackers look for (open AJAX and REST handlers, SQL built from request data, unsafe uploads, secret keys in the code), as leads for a developer.
  • What visitors see. In full scans it reads the home page, the newest posts and pages, and the cart and checkout as a visitor gets them: scripts from new or blocklisted hosts, known malware campaigns such as fake CAPTCHA pages, and secret keys printed into the page source.
  • Updates and hardening. A PHP version that no longer gets security fixes, premium plugins whose own updater offers an update you haven’t installed, weak keys, open registration with a powerful role, error messages shown to visitors, administrators without 2FA, an over-privileged database user, files anyone can download, missing HTTPS and security headers, and more.

What you get

  • Fix first. Signs of compromise and the most severe problems go to the top.
  • A grade you can trust. A site with an open critical problem can’t score better than D.
  • Every finding explained. Why it matters, how to fix it, and the evidence the check saw, with secrets masked.
  • A report to share. A print-friendly page of the grade and every open finding, to print or save as PDF.
  • Email alerts. Optionally, an email when a scan finds a new critical or high problem.
  • WP-CLI. Run scans and list findings from the command line.

How it works

Nothing runs on your site’s front end. Scans run in short steps from the dashboard, WP-Cron or WP-CLI (wp shieldxen scan), so they work on shared hosting. Every feature is in this plugin, free. There is no account to create.

ShieldXen reports problems. It doesn’t remove malware, restore files or block attacks.

A clean scan isn’t proof a site is clean. The dashboard lists what a scan can’t see.

External services

This plugin connects only to wordpress.org, and only during full and file scans:

  • api.wordpress.org, for the checksums of the WordPress version you run, to find changed core files. It sends the version and the site’s language. Terms and privacy: https://wordpress.org/about/privacy/
  • downloads.wordpress.org, for the checksum file and the release zip of each installed plugin and theme that comes from wordpress.org, to find changed files. It sends the plugin’s or theme’s name and version, and only when its files changed since the last check or a week has passed. A zip is downloaded to a temporary file, read without being unpacked, and deleted; each version is downloaded once. Only plugins and themes that WordPress’s own update check found on wordpress.org are asked about. Never sent: what you marked as your own code or a vendor’s, and plugins that declare they update from somewhere else (an “Update URI”). Terms and privacy: https://wordpress.org/about/privacy/

The malware signatures and the other detection data ship inside the plugin; nothing is downloaded to update them. No request follows a redirect, and every one checks the server’s certificate. The plugin also requests pages and files of your own site (the HTTP and live page checks), which stay between the site and itself. When the site’s own certificate fails, those requests report it as a finding and go on checking the pages without verifying it; requests to other servers never do.

Source code

Everything in the plugin is its readable source, including the detection data in data/ (JSON), except the admin screens’ built script and styles in assets/build. Their full readable source ships beside them, in assets/src (React, with @wordpress/scripts). To rebuild assets/build from it, run these in the plugin’s folder: npm install, then npm run build.
sections.installation:
1. In your admin, go to Plugins > Add New Plugin, search for “ShieldXen” and click Install Now, or upload the plugin’s zip under Upload Plugin.
  2. Activate it. On multisite, network-activate it from the network admin.
  3. Open Security in the admin menu and run your first scan.

You can also scan from WP-CLI: wp shieldxen scan.
sections.faq:
Is ShieldXen free?

Yes. Every feature described here is in this plugin. There is no paid version and no account to create.

Does it slow my site down?

No. It adds nothing to the pages visitors load. Scans run in the background in short steps.

Does it send my data anywhere?

No. Scan results stay in your site’s database. To compare your files with the official copies it asks wordpress.org for the checksums of the versions you run (see “External services”); your files are never uploaded.

Does it remove malware or block attacks?

No. ShieldXen finds and explains problems, ranks them and tells you how to fix each one. Removing malware and blocking attacks are left to you, your host or a firewall.

What does the grade mean?

Every scan starts at 100 points. Each open problem takes points away, more for severe ones, and the total gives a letter from A to F. While a critical problem is open the grade can’t be better than D, and while a high one is open, not better than C.

If a scan finds nothing, is my site clean?

Not necessarily. A scan finds what its checks look for, in the files, settings and pages it can reach. New malware, or code that only wakes up for some requests, can pass. The dashboard lists what a scan can’t see.

Can I scan from the command line?

Yes. wp shieldxen scan runs a full scan; add --type=quick, files, database, vulns or hardening for a narrower one, and --format=json or csv for scripts. wp shieldxen findings lists what’s open.

Why do scheduled scans run late?

WP-Cron only runs when someone visits the site. A real cron job makes scans and alerts run on time.

Does it work on multisite?

Yes, network-activated. The files and users belong to the whole network, so the plugin checks them once, from the main site, and its screen is in the network admin. The database and live page checks cover the main site. Subsite administrators don’t see it.
sections.changelog:
1.0.0 – 2026-11-17

  • Initial release.
  • Files: core, plugin and theme integrity against the official copies, malware signatures, a change watch for your own code, and checks for PHP where it doesn’t belong, downloadable backups and logs, and old WordPress copies.
  • Database: hidden scripts and spam, hidden administrators and plugins, unexpected accounts and application passwords, code in options, snippets and scheduled tasks, and account-recreating triggers.
  • Your own code: quick checks for open AJAX and REST handlers, SQL built from request data, unsafe uploads and secret keys.
  • Live pages: new and blocklisted script hosts, known malware campaigns, and secret keys in the page source.
  • Updates and hardening: PHP end of life, updates offered by premium plugins’ own updaters, and settings checks.
  • The dashboard with the grade and the fix-first list, findings with evidence, scan history, a printable report, email alerts, a dashboard widget and WP-CLI.

short_description: Scans files, database and live pages for malware and backdoors, ranks what to fix first, and grades your site. No account needed.
